title: Baseline Risk Assessment (Extract)
subtitle: Hazard register for the Kya Sand bakery, signed 16 February 2026

rows: Bakery at 41 Bernie Street, Kya Sand, Randburg: flour receiving and storage, mixing, dividing and moulding, baking, packing, cleaning, dispatch and maintenance. 88 employees on two shifts.
Karabo Mokoena, registered health and safety practitioner, appointed in writing as risk assessor on 12 January 2026 (appointment and registration filed in Section B)

Deon Swanepoel, Production Manager; Gift Mathebula, Maintenance Foreman; Zanele Khumalo, health and safety representative, mixing and baking; Ayesha Patel, health and safety representative, packing and dispatch

Walk through of every area and task, talks with the people doing the work, and a review of the incident register for 2025. Each risk is rated as likelihood (1 rare to 5 almost certain) times severity (1 first aid case to 5 fatality or permanent disability): 1 to 6 low, 8 to 12 medium, 15 to 25 high. Controls are chosen in the order elimination, substitution, engineering, administrative, then protective equipment.

cols: Controls, in the order of the hierarchy
rows: 1. Flour dust in mixing and when tipping bags: breathing problems and skin irritation

**Substitution:** bulk flour silo feed replaces hand tipping on mixers 1 and 2. **Engineering:** local exhaust ventilation at the tipping station. **Administrative:** no dry sweeping; vacuum cleaning; exposure monitoring by an approved inspection authority. **Protective equipment:** respirators fit tested for bag tipping.
2. Hot ovens, trays and racks: burns
**Engineering:** oven door guards and rack stops. **Administrative:** hot surface signs; safe work procedure for loading ovens. **Protective equipment:** heat resistant gloves and sleeves.
3. Moving parts of mixers and dividers during cleaning: crushing and amputation
**Engineering:** interlocked guards on every mixer and divider. **Administrative:** lockout before cleaning or clearing a blockage; only trained operators; daily guard check by the supervisor.
4. Forklifts and pedestrians at the dispatch dock: being struck

**Engineering:** barriers and marked walkways that keep pedestrians out of the loading bay; blue spot lights on forklifts. **Administrative:** no pedestrians in the loading bay while loading is under way; trained and authorised operators only; daily pre use checks; speed limit.
5. Lifting 25 kg flour bags and full trays: back and shoulder injuries
**Engineering:** bag lift assist at the small batch mixer; trolleys for trays. **Administrative:** team lifts; manual handling training; job rotation every two hours.
6. Cleaning chemicals, including caustic oven cleaner: burns to skin and eyes

**Substitution:** milder degreaser for daily cleaning. **Engineering:** dosing unit for dilution. **Administrative:** safety data sheets at the chemical store; chemical handling training. **Protective equipment:** goggles, gloves and aprons; eyewash station.
7. Wet and floury floors: slips and falls
**Engineering:** slip resistant flooring in the wash area. **Administrative:** clean as you go; wet floor signs. **Protective equipment:** slip resistant safety shoes.

blocks.p: The draft register was discussed at the health and safety committee meeting of **11 February 2026** and at toolbox talks on both shifts on **12 and 13 February 2026**, attended by 79 employees (registers filed in Section D). Employees asked for a second eyewash station at the wash bay and for job rotation on the packing line; both were added. The health and safety representatives walked the site with the risk assessor and signed below.

This assessment is reviewed every year, and sooner after an incident, a new machine, a new substance, a change in a process or a request from the health and safety committee. Issue based and task based risk assessments are filed with it in Section C.
